issues.legal_issue: A judgment debtor may obtain debt-redemption relief when the applicants are agriculturists and the decree arises from a qualifying loan, including where a co-obligor was not assessed to income tax when the advance was made and was not then liable to such assessment.
material_facts: The applicants sought relief to recalculate and amend a mortgage decree under the debt-redemption legislation.
The applicants were agriculturists when they brought the original suit and when they applied for relief; the decree had been passed before the legislation commenced.

One co-obligor earned a salary below the then-applicable taxable minimum when the advance was made. The taxable minimum was reduced only after the advance, and income tax was first deducted from his salary afterward.
The other judgment debtors were admitted to be agriculturists, and the advance was secured by the mortgage concerned.
issues.conclusion: The judgment debtors were entitled to the benefit of the Act. Even assuming the statutory proviso required the advance to have been made to an agriculturist, the co-obligor was an agriculturist when the advance was made because he was neither assessed nor liable to income tax at that time.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 8, an agriculturist or workman liable under a decree to which the Act applies may seek amendment of a pre-commencement decree. Sections 2(6) and 2(17) make the decree eligible where it was passed in a suit relating to a loan, and section 2(9) defines loan and contains a proviso concerning advances made to agriculturists. Agriculturist status is determined under section 2(3), including its income-tax qualification. On the facts, the applicable taxable minimum had not yet been reduced when the advance was made, so the co-obligor was not then liable to assessment. The Court did not decide whether the proviso to section 2(9) applied or whether the Full Bench decision in Ketki Kunwar v. Ram Saroop was correct; it assumed the proviso applied for purposes of its decision.

rule.if: debt_redemption_decree_application and applicants_are_agriculturists_when_applying and decree_predates_relief_law and decree_arises_from_qualifying_advance and (co_obligor_not_assessed_when_advance_made and co_obligor_not_then_taxable)

predicates.debt_redemption_decree_application: A judgment debtor applies in a proceeding seeking debt-redemption relief to recalculate or amend a decree.
predicates.applicants_are_agriculturists_when_apply: The applicants seeking relief are agriculturists when they make the application.
predicates.decree_predates_relief_law: The decree for which amendment is sought was passed before the debt-relief law commenced.
predicates.decree_arises_from_qualifying_advance: The decree was passed in a suit relating to an advance that qualifies as a loan under the debt-relief law.
predicates.co_obligor_not_assessed_when_advance_mad: A co-obligor was not assessed to income tax when the advance was made.
predicates.co_obligor_not_then_taxable: At the time of the advance, the co-obligor's income was below the then-applicable taxable minimum, and no law then made that income taxable.
predicates.judgment_debtors_are_entitled_to_debt_re: The judgment debtors may obtain the debt-relief benefits sought.

issues.definition: When agriculturist judgment debtors seek amendment of a pre-law decree arising from a qualifying advance, and a co-obligor was neither assessed nor taxable when the advance was made, they are entitled to debt relief.

issues.legal_issue: An appellant may not raise for the first time at the final appellate stage a factual objection that was not pleaded in the initial objection and was not urged in the intermediate appeal, particularly when deciding it requires factual investigation.
material_facts: The decree-holders' initial objection did not dispute that the mortgagees under the earlier and later mortgages were the same for purposes of the judgment debtors' accounts.
The trial court found that the mortgagees were the same as regards the judgment debtors.
Although the decree-holders alleged in their intermediate appeal that the mortgagees differed, they did not specifically urge that contention there.
The contention would have required investigation into the facts and was raised at the final appellate stage.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to permit the decree-holders to raise the factual contention at that stage.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that, in the circumstances, it was not right to allow a factual question requiring investigation to be raised at the final appellate stage when it had not been pleaded in the objection and had not been urged before the intermediate appellate court.

rule.if: final_appeal and factual_objection_requires_investigation and not pleaded_in_initial_objection and not urged_in_intermediate_appeal

predicates.final_appeal: The matter is before a court hearing the final appeal.
predicates.factual_objection_requires_investigation: The objection depends on disputed facts that require investigation.
predicates.pleaded_in_initial_objection: The appellant included the factual objection in its initial objection to the relief application.
predicates.urged_in_intermediate_appeal: The appellant specifically argued the factual objection before the intermediate appellate court.
predicates.final_appellate_court_refuses_new_factua: The final appellate court does not allow the appellant to raise the factual objection at that stage.

issues.definition: In a final appeal, a factual objection requiring investigation is refused when it was omitted from the initial objection and was not urged in the intermediate appeal.
